APX-000032.transcript:
Customer (James Martin): There's a crew digging up the street outside my house and I never got any notice about it.
Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): Hi James Martin, Nomsa Khumalo here — let me pull that up.
Customer (James Martin): Who do I actually call if the crew damages something on my property?
Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): Thanks for letting us know. Let me check the project schedule for your street.
Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): Which street and block is the crew working on?
Customer (James Martin): It's our house, right where they've got the fencing up.
Customer (James Martin): Is my gas service going to be interrupted at any point during this work?
Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): Has anyone from the crew spoken to you yet?
Customer (James Martin): No, they just started digging.
Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): Do you need driveway access during the day?
Customer (James Martin): Yes, I leave for work at seven.
Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): Is anyone at home who relies on the gas during the day?
Customer (James Martin): My mother's home most days, and she needs the heat on.
Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): Let me take a look. I've looked up the System Betterment Program schedule for that street segment and confirmed the notification timeline that was sent.
Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): This is the System Betterment Program, replacing older steel pipe on your street. A notice with the timeline and a site contact should have gone out two weeks ahead.
Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): This is the pre-1975 pipe replacement work under our System Betterment Program — a notice with the timeline and a site contact number should have gone out two weeks ahead, I've resent it to your address and confirmed there's no planned service interruption.
Customer (James Martin): How long will the street be dug up?
Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): About two weeks on your block, with the road restored after.
Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): To recap: two weeks on your block, a door knock before any interruption, and the notice with the site contact is in your email.
Customer (James Martin): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Customer (Robert Bell): My estimated bill was way higher than what I actually used last month.
Agent (Naledi Nkosi): Hi Robert Bell, Naledi Nkosi here — let me pull that up.

Customer (Robert Bell): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Naledi Nkosi): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Customer (Robert Grant): So my total won't go up much?
Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): It shouldn't. Most of this month's jump is colder weather, not the rate change.
Customer (Robert Grant): Can I get that in writing?
Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): The AUC summary and your usage figure are in your email now.
Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): To recap, everything's noted on your file, and the team will follow up with you.
Customer (Robert Grant): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Customer (Mark Reid): I got a letter about a 'Rate 1' and 'Rate 2' change and I have no idea what it means for my bill.
Agent (Naledi Nkosi): Hi Mark Reid, Naledi Nkosi here — let me pull that up.
Customer (Mark Reid): Is this the Phase 2 thing the AUC approved, or did I do something wrong on my account?
Agent (Naledi Nkosi): Good question, a lot of customers are asking about this one. Let me check your account.
Agent (Naledi Nkosi): Can you give me the account number from your bill, or the service address and the name on the account?
Customer (Mark Reid): Sure, it's the house on the account, and the bill's in my name.
Customer (Mark Reid): I've been on the same rate for years, why is this changing now?
Agent (Naledi Nkosi): Roughly how much gas do you use in a year, or should I look it up?
Customer (Mark Reid): No idea. Can you look it up?
Agent (Naledi Nkosi): Do you have any irrigation or shop meters on the same account?
Customer (Mark Reid): No, just the house.
Agent (Naledi Nkosi): Let me take a look. I've pulled up the account, confirmed the Rate 1/Rate 2 threshold under the August 1 Phase 2 restructuring, and walked through what changed on this specific account.
Agent (Naledi Nkosi): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Naledi Nkosi): Since August 1, Rate 1 covers accounts using under 4,000 GJ a year and Rate 2 covers larger users. The AUC approved it as Phase 2 of the rate restructuring.
Agent (Naledi Nkosi): Your usage puts you right at the edge of the new Rate 2 threshold, so this bill reflects the higher rate class — I don't have authority to move you back to Rate 1 manually, that's set by your metered usage under the AUC-approved structure.
Customer (Mark Reid): Can't you just put me back on Rate 1?
Agent (Naledi Nkosi): Not manually. The class follows your metered usage under the approved structure.
Agent (Naledi Nkosi): To recap: your usage puts you in Rate 2 for now, the class is reviewed against annual usage, and the details are in your email.
Customer (Mark Reid): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Naledi Nkosi): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): Hi Megan Murray, Nomsa Khumalo here — let me pull that up.
Customer (Megan Murray): Is this the Phase 2 thing the AUC approved, or did I do something wrong on my account?
Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): Good question, a lot of customers are asking about this one. Let me check your account.
Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): Before I go into the account, can you confirm the service address and the account holder's name?
Customer (Megan Murray): Sure, it's the house on the account, and the bill's in my name.
Customer (Megan Murray): I've been on the same rate for years, why is this changing now?
Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): Is this a home, a farm, or a business account?
Customer (Megan Murray): It's our home. We're not a business.
Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): Roughly how much gas do you use in a year, or should I look it up?
Customer (Megan Murray): No idea. Can you look it up?

Customer (Megan Murray): Can't you just put me back on Rate 1?
Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): Not manually. The class follows your metered usage under the approved structure.
Customer (Megan Murray): What happens if my usage drops next year?
Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): The class is reviewed against your annual usage, so it would move back if you fall under the threshold. I've noted that on the account.
Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): To recap: your usage puts you in Rate 2 for now, the class is reviewed against annual usage, and the details are in your email.
Customer (Megan Murray): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Nomsa Khumalo): Thanks for bearing with me. Everything's noted on your file, and you'll hear back as I said.

APX-000436.transcript:
Customer (David Thompson): Can you explain how the equalization plan works out my monthly amount?
Agent (Lerato Ndlovu): Hi David Thompson, Lerato Ndlovu here — let me pull that up.
Customer (David Thompson): This is the third time this year my equalized amount has changed on me.
Agent (Lerato Ndlovu): Thanks for bearing with us on this. Let me go through the bill with you properly.
Agent (Lerato Ndlovu): Before I go into the account, can you confirm the service address and the account holder's name?
Customer (David Thompson): Sure, it's the house on the account, and the bill's in my name.
Customer (David Thompson): If the point of this plan is predictable payments, why does it keep moving?
Agent (Lerato Ndlovu): Did you get a notice before the amount changed?
Customer (David Thompson): No. I found out when the payment came out.
Agent (Lerato Ndlovu): Has anything changed at home, like a new appliance or more people?
Customer (David Thompson): We had a baby, so the heat's been on more.
Agent (Lerato Ndlovu): Would you rather stay on the plan or go back to regular billing?
Customer (David Thompson): Stay on it, if it stops jumping around.
Agent (Lerato Ndlovu): Let me take a look. I've reviewed the equalization plan's 12-month usage average and the reconciliation adjustment that triggered the change.
Agent (Lerato Ndlovu): Thanks for holding — I've got the full picture now.
Agent (Lerato Ndlovu): The plan averages your last twelve months of usage and is reviewed at month six. If usage runs higher than the estimate, the difference is added.
Agent (Lerato Ndlovu): The equalization amount is recalculated from your usage history under the plan terms, and I can't reverse an adjustment that's already been applied — what I can do is flag your file so the next change comes with a heads-up call before it hits your bill.
Customer (David Thompson): So the CA$600 is still due?
Agent (Lerato Ndlovu): The adjustment has been applied and I can't reverse it. I can split it over two payments instead of one.
Agent (Lerato Ndlovu): To recap: the adjustment stands, it can be split over two payments, and your file is flagged for a call before the next change.
Customer (David Thompson): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Lerato Ndlovu): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

APX-000440.transcript:
Customer (Tyler Young): My bill jumped and I don't understand why. Did something change with my rate?
Agent (Karabo Zulu): Hi Tyler Young, Karabo Zulu here — let me pull that up.
Customer (Tyler Young): Is this the Phase 2 thing the AUC approved, or did I do something wrong on my account?
Agent (Karabo Zulu): Good question, a lot of customers are asking about this one. Let me check your account.
Agent (Karabo Zulu): Can you give me the account number from your bill, or the service address and the name on the account?
Customer (Tyler Young): Yes, same address as always, and the account's under my name.
Customer (Tyler Young): I've been on the same rate for years, why is this changing now?
Agent (Karabo Zulu): Is this a home, a farm, or a business account?
Customer (Tyler Young): It's our home. We're not a business.
Agent (Karabo Zulu): Do you have any irrigation or shop meters on the same account?
Customer (Tyler Young): No, just the house.
Agent (Karabo Zulu): Let me take a look. I've pulled up the account, confirmed the Rate 1/Rate 2 threshold under the August 1 Phase 2 restructuring, and walked through what changed on this specific account.
Agent (Karabo Zulu): Thanks for holding — I've got the full picture now.
Agent (Karabo Zulu): Since August 1, Rate 1 covers accounts using under 4,000 GJ a year and Rate 2 covers larger users. The AUC approved it as Phase 2 of the rate restructuring.
Agent (Karabo Zulu): You're on Rate 1 since your annual usage is under 4,000 GJ, so the main change is the way the distribution charge is broken out on the bill — your total shouldn't move much. I've sent the AUC decision summary to your email so you have it on file.
Customer (Tyler Young): So my total won't go up much?
Agent (Karabo Zulu): It shouldn't. Most of this month's jump is colder weather, not the rate change.
Agent (Karabo Zulu): To recap: you're staying on Rate 1, the change is mostly how the bill is laid out, and the summary is in your email.
Customer (Tyler Young): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Karabo Zulu): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Customer (Megan Morrison): Our furnace takes a few seconds to light after the fan starts. Is that a problem?
Agent (Vusi Jacobs): Hi Megan Morrison, Vusi Jacobs here — let me pull that up.
Customer (Megan Morrison): Is this something I should be worried about, or is it normal?

Agent (Vusi Jacobs): To recap: the ignition sound is normal, a yearly service is worth booking, and the emergency line is there if you ever smell gas.
Customer (Megan Morrison): Alright, thank you for looking into it.

Customer (Susan Reid): My bill jumped and I don't understand why. Did something change with my rate?
Agent (Lerato Ndlovu): Hi Susan Reid, Lerato Ndlovu here — let me pull that up.
Customer (Susan Reid): Is this the Phase 2 thing the AUC approved, or did I do something wrong on my account?
Agent (Lerato Ndlovu): Good question, a lot of customers are asking about this one. Let me check your account.
Agent (Lerato Ndlovu): Can you give me the account number from your bill, or the service address and the name on the account?

Customer (Susan Reid): No idea. Can you look it up?
Agent (Lerato Ndlovu): Did you get the letter by mail or by email?
Customer (Susan Reid): By mail, a couple of weeks ago.
Agent (Lerato Ndlovu): Do you have any irrigation or shop meters on the same account?
Customer (Susan Reid): No, just the house.
Agent (Lerato Ndlovu): Let me take a look. I've pulled up the account, confirmed the Rate 1/Rate 2 threshold under the August 1 Phase 2 restructuring, and walked through what changed on this specific account.
Agent (Lerato Ndlovu): Okay, I've got it pulled up now.
Agent (Lerato Ndlovu): Since August 1, Rate 1 covers accounts using under 4,000 GJ a year and Rate 2 covers larger users. The AUC approved it as Phase 2 of the rate restructuring.
Agent (Lerato Ndlovu): Your usage puts you right at the edge of the new Rate 2 threshold, so this bill reflects the higher rate class — I don't have authority to move you back to Rate 1 manually, that's set by your metered usage under the AUC-approved structure.
Customer (Susan Reid): Can't you just put me back on Rate 1?
Agent (Lerato Ndlovu): Not manually. The class follows your metered usage under the approved structure.
Agent (Lerato Ndlovu): To recap: your usage puts you in Rate 2 for now, the class is reviewed against annual usage, and the details are in your email.
Customer (Susan Reid): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Lerato Ndlovu): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Customer (Mark Murray): Can you explain how the equalization plan works out my monthly amount?
Agent (Vusi Jacobs): Hi Mark Murray, Vusi Jacobs here — let me pull that up.
Customer (Mark Murray): This is the third time this year my equalized amount has changed on me.
Agent (Vusi Jacobs): Understood. Let me pull up the account and look at the charges before I say anything.
Agent (Vusi Jacobs): Before I go into the account, can you confirm the service address and the account holder's name?
Customer (Mark Murray): Sure, it's the house on the account, and the bill's in my name.
Customer (Mark Murray): If the point of this plan is predictable payments, why does it keep moving?
Agent (Vusi Jacobs): When did you first join the equalization plan?
Customer (Mark Murray): About two years ago, when we moved in.
Agent (Vusi Jacobs): Did you get a notice before the amount changed?
Customer (Mark Murray): No. I found out when the payment came out.
Agent (Vusi Jacobs): Would you rather stay on the plan or go back to regular billing?
Customer (Mark Murray): Stay on it, if it stops jumping around.
Agent (Vusi Jacobs): Let me take a look. I've reviewed the equalization plan's 12-month usage average and the reconciliation adjustment that triggered the change.
Agent (Vusi Jacobs): Thanks for holding — I've got the full picture now.
Agent (Vusi Jacobs): The plan averages your last twelve months of usage and is reviewed at month six. If usage runs higher than the estimate, the difference is added.
Agent (Vusi Jacobs): Your usage this year is running above last year's, which is why the amount went up.
Customer (Mark Murray): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Vusi Jacobs): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Vusi Jacobs): The plan recalculates twice a year against your rolling usage average, and this adjustment reflects higher usage than last year's estimate — I've set up an email alert so you'll get advance notice before the next recalculation instead of finding out on the bill.
Customer (Mark Murray): Will it change again without warning?
Agent (Vusi Jacobs): The next review is in six months, and you'll get an email two weeks before it.
Customer (Mark Murray): And the catch-up amount?
Agent (Vusi Jacobs): I've spread it over your remaining months so there's no lump sum.
Agent (Vusi Jacobs): To recap, everything's noted on your file, and the team will follow up with you.
Customer (Mark Murray): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Vusi Jacobs): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Customer (Karen Ross): I got a letter about a 'Rate 1' and 'Rate 2' change and I have no idea what it means for my bill.
Agent (Karabo Zulu): Hi Karen Ross, Karabo Zulu here — let me pull that up.
Customer (Karen Ross): I've been on the same rate for years, why is this changing now?
Agent (Karabo Zulu): Good question, a lot of customers are asking about this one. Let me check your account.
Agent (Karabo Zulu): Can you give me the account number from your bill, or the service address and the name on the account?
Customer (Karen Ross): Sure, it's the house on the account, and the bill's in my name.
Customer (Karen Ross): Is this the Phase 2 thing the AUC approved, or did I do something wrong on my account?
Agent (Karabo Zulu): Is this a home, a farm, or a business account?
Customer (Karen Ross): It's our home. We're not a business.
Agent (Karabo Zulu): Roughly how much gas do you use in a year, or should I look it up?
Customer (Karen Ross): No idea. Can you look it up?
Agent (Karabo Zulu): Let me take a look. I've pulled up the account, confirmed the Rate 1/Rate 2 threshold under the August 1 Phase 2 restructuring, and walked through what changed on this specific account.
Agent (Karabo Zulu): Okay, I've got it pulled up now.
Agent (Karabo Zulu): Since August 1, Rate 1 covers accounts using under 4,000 GJ a year and Rate 2 covers larger users. The AUC approved it as Phase 2 of the rate restructuring.
Agent (Karabo Zulu): You're on Rate 1 since your annual usage is under 4,000 GJ, so the main change is the way the distribution charge is broken out on the bill — your total shouldn't move much. I've sent the AUC decision summary to your email so you have it on file.
Customer (Karen Ross): So my total won't go up much?
Agent (Karabo Zulu): It shouldn't. Most of this month's jump is colder weather, not the rate change.
Agent (Karabo Zulu): To recap: you're staying on Rate 1, the change is mostly how the bill is laid out, and the summary is in your email.

Customer (Amanda Baker): I need to close my account at the old address and set up payments for the new one.

Customer (Michael Fraser): I'm following up again — someone told me I'm being moved to a different rate class because of the August rate change. Is that true?

Customer (Michael Fraser): I already explained this on my last contact.

Customer (Michael Fraser): Is this the Phase 2 thing the AUC approved, or did I do something wrong on my account?

Agent (Vusi Jacobs): Since August 1, Rate 1 covers accounts using under 4,000 GJ a year and Rate 2 covers larger users. The AUC approved it as Phase 2 of the rate restructuring.
Agent (Vusi Jacobs): Your usage puts you right at the edge of the new Rate 2 threshold, so this bill reflects the higher rate class — I don't have authority to move you back to Rate 1 manually, that's set by your metered usage under the AUC-approved structure.
Customer (Michael Fraser): Can't you just put me back on Rate 1?
Agent (Vusi Jacobs): Not manually. The class follows your metered usage under the approved structure.
Agent (Vusi Jacobs): To recap: your usage puts you in Rate 2 for now, the class is reviewed against annual usage, and the details are in your email.
Customer (Michael Fraser): That's not really the answer I was hoping for, but okay.
Agent (Vusi Jacobs): I've logged everything here so if this comes up again, the next agent has the full picture.

Customer (David Kerr): I'm following up again — the pipe replacement crew is on my street, and nobody told me how long it will take.

APX-000670.transcript:
Customer (Brian Martin): I'm following up again — my bill jumped and I don't understand why. Did something change with my rate?
Agent (Naledi Nkosi): Hi Brian Martin, Naledi Nkosi here — let me pull that up.
Customer (Brian Martin): I already explained this on my last contact.
Agent (Naledi Nkosi): I'm sorry about that — let me look at what happened last time and pick up from there.
Customer (Brian Martin): I've been on the same rate for years, why is this changing now?
Agent (Naledi Nkosi): Good question, a lot of customers are asking about this one. Let me check your account.
Agent (Naledi Nkosi): Can you give me the account number from your bill, or the service address and the name on the account?
Customer (Brian Martin): Yes, same address as always, and the account's under my name.
Customer (Brian Martin): Is this the Phase 2 thing the AUC approved, or did I do something wrong on my account?
Agent (Naledi Nkosi): Did you get the letter by mail or by email?
Customer (Brian Martin): By mail, a couple of weeks ago.
Agent (Naledi Nkosi): Do you have any irrigation or shop meters on the same account?
Customer (Brian Martin): No, just the house.
Agent (Naledi Nkosi): Let me take a look. I've pulled up the account, confirmed the Rate 1/Rate 2 threshold under the August 1 Phase 2 restructuring, and walked through what changed on this specific account.
Agent (Naledi Nkosi): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Naledi Nkosi): Since August 1, Rate 1 covers accounts using under 4,000 GJ a year and Rate 2 covers larger users. The AUC approved it as Phase 2 of the rate restructuring.
Agent (Naledi Nkosi): Your usage puts you right at the edge of the new Rate 2 threshold, so this bill reflects the higher rate class — I don't have authority to move you back to Rate 1 manually, that's set by your metered usage under the AUC-approved structure.
Customer (Brian Martin): Can't you just put me back on Rate 1?
Agent (Naledi Nkosi): Not manually. The class follows your metered usage under the approved structure.
Agent (Naledi Nkosi): To recap: your usage puts you in Rate 2 for now, the class is reviewed against annual usage, and the details are in your email.
Customer (Brian Martin): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Naledi Nkosi): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

APX-000771.transcript:
Customer (Linda Campbell): I'm following up again — someone told me I'm being moved to a different rate class because of the August rate change. Is that true?
Agent (Vusi Jacobs): Hi Linda Campbell, Vusi Jacobs here — let me pull that up.
Customer (Linda Campbell): I already explained this on my last contact.
Agent (Vusi Jacobs): I'm sorry about that — let me look at what happened last time and pick up from there.
Customer (Linda Campbell): Is this the Phase 2 thing the AUC approved, or did I do something wrong on my account?
Agent (Vusi Jacobs): Good question, a lot of customers are asking about this one. Let me check your account.
Agent (Vusi Jacobs): Can you give me the account number from your bill, or the service address and the name on the account?
Customer (Linda Campbell): Yes, same address as always, and the account's under my name.
Customer (Linda Campbell): I've been on the same rate for years, why is this changing now?
Agent (Vusi Jacobs): Is this a home, a farm, or a business account?
Customer (Linda Campbell): It's our home. We're not a business.
Agent (Vusi Jacobs): Did you get the letter by mail or by email?
Customer (Linda Campbell): By mail, a couple of weeks ago.
Agent (Vusi Jacobs): Let me take a look. I've pulled up the account, confirmed the Rate 1/Rate 2 threshold under the August 1 Phase 2 restructuring, and walked through what changed on this specific account.
Agent (Vusi Jacobs): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Vusi Jacobs): Since August 1, Rate 1 covers accounts using under 4,000 GJ a year and Rate 2 covers larger users. The AUC approved it as Phase 2 of the rate restructuring.
Agent (Vusi Jacobs): Your usage puts you right at the edge of the new Rate 2 threshold, so this bill reflects the higher rate class — I don't have authority to move you back to Rate 1 manually, that's set by your metered usage under the AUC-approved structure.
Customer (Linda Campbell): Can't you just put me back on Rate 1?
Agent (Vusi Jacobs): Not manually. The class follows your metered usage under the approved structure.
Agent (Vusi Jacobs): To recap: your usage puts you in Rate 2 for now, the class is reviewed against annual usage, and the details are in your email.
Customer (Linda Campbell): That's not really the answer I was hoping for, but okay.
Agent (Vusi Jacobs): I've logged everything here so if this comes up again, the next agent has the full picture.

Customer (Nicole Kerr): I'm following up again — there's a crew digging up the street outside my house and I never got any notice about it.
Agent (Naledi Nkosi): Hi Nicole Kerr, Naledi Nkosi here — let me pull that up.
Customer (Nicole Kerr): I already explained this on my last contact.
Agent (Naledi Nkosi): I'm sorry about that — let me look at what happened last time and pick up from there.
Customer (Nicole Kerr): Who do I actually call if the crew damages something on my property?

Customer (Nicole Kerr): It's our house, right where they've got the fencing up.

Agent (Naledi Nkosi): This is the System Betterment Program, replacing older steel pipe on your street. A notice with the timeline and a site contact should have gone out two weeks ahead.

Agent (Naledi Nkosi): The work is confirmed as part of the System Betterment Program, but the notification that should have gone out ahead of the crew arriving didn't reach your address — I've logged that gap for the notifications team, though I can't change the schedule already in progress.
Customer (Nicole Kerr): So the notice just never came?
Agent (Naledi Nkosi): It didn't reach your address, and I've logged that for the notifications team.
Agent (Naledi Nkosi): To recap: the missed notice is logged, the site supervisor will call you about access, and the schedule itself stays as planned.
Customer (Nicole Kerr): That's not really the answer I was hoping for, but okay.
Agent (Naledi Nkosi): I've logged everything here so if this comes up again, the next agent has the full picture.
